source.title: Data Scaling Laws for Imitation Learning-Based End-to-End Autonomous Driving
source.authors: Yu-Peng Zheng; Peng-Xuan Yang; Zhong-Pu Xia; Qi-Chao Zhang; Yu-Hang Zheng; Bu Jin; Teng Zhang; Ben Lu; Chao Han; Wei-Ze Li; Song-En Gu; Xian-Peng Lang; Xiang-Yuan Lan; Dong-Bin Zhao

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure data are only available as figure/OCR content.
record.tranche_reason: It investigates data scaling in imitation-learning-based autonomous driving, a new application setting, and reports open- and closed-loop results.
record.gate_note: The paper directly tests scaling with training-data quantity in autonomous driving. Its cited results about language-model and other-domain scaling laws are not this study's results. The paper describes six dataset sizes in the setup/table but says five models were used for the open-loop fit.
record.test_reason: It trains the same driving model on 10k to 4M demonstrations and fits a power law to held-out open-loop trajectory error (ADE). This is a data-scaling test in a new regime: imitation-learning autonomous driving. It does not vary parameters or compute.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find open-loop ADE follows a power law in data, but closed-loop performance does not. They say data distribution matters: targeted long-tail data helps at fixed total size. They report combinatorial generalization as data scales. Their claim that targeted augmentation beats indiscriminate expansion is not tested against an equal-size indiscriminate baseline.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales demonstration data for imitation-learning autonomous driving and measures trajectory ADE and closed-loop driving scores; it does not reproduce language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Evaluation setting changes the reported scaling pattern: open-loop ADE follows a fitted power law, whereas closed-loop performance does not. The paper also reports that closed-loop metric trends differ from one another.

fits_no_version.finding: Closed-loop driving scores (safety, comfort, rule, efficiency, navigation, total) rise with data but do not follow the open-loop power law. Safety and comfort gains slow after 200k–700k demonstrations, and the rule score is unstable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In imitation-learning driving, deployment (closed-loop) performance is not predicted by a power law in data, even when held-out trajectory error is.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed total data, raising the share of two poorly performing long-tail scenarios cut their open-loop ADE by 9.7–32.9%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed dataset size, reallocating data toward weak scenarios improves performance on those scenarios.

fits_no_version.finding: For two held-out scenario categories, the ADE gap to similar seen scenarios narrows from 50k to 2M demonstrations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling imitation data yields combinatorial generalization to unseen driving scenarios.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The authors note that the closed-loop environment is not fully aligned with the open-loop setting, limiting direct comparison. The paper says five models were used for the open-loop fit, while the setup and resource table list six dataset sizes.

untested.parts: Not tested: there is no language-model pretraining loss.
Not tested: there is no extrapolation from small fits to larger runs.
Not tested: model size is never varied and there is no compute-optimal allocation.
Not tested: no architecture shape is varied.
Only data-quantity scaling of open-loop ADE in driving is tested. Parameter and compute scaling, other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested.
Not tested for language models. The closed-loop driving scores are recorded under fits_no_version.
Not tested: no comparison of fitting methods, schedules, parameter counting or exponents.

missing.what: Per-size ADE values behind the fit and the closed-loop score values; neither is legible in the text.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V5 'challenges' label and both V7 labels are dropped. The closed-loop scores are task outcomes, not a loss, and the open-loop vs closed-loop contrast is a difference of metric, not a fitting choice. There is one model architecture only, no uncertainty is reported, and the closed-loop environment is not aligned with the open-loop test set (per the authors). The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests driving-data quantity, not held-out language-model pretraining loss or scaling in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Does not fit language-model scaling laws on small runs and test predictions on much larger runs.
Does not vary model parameters and tokens under fixed compute or estimate compute-optimal allocation.
Does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at a fixed parameter count.

Tests data-quantity scaling in imitation-learning autonomous driving, not image/video generation, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, or other modalities and regimes. It does not test parameter- or compute-scaling laws.
Does not test downstream tasks of language models or relate downstream performance to language-model pretraining loss.
The open-/closed-loop results differ, but the study does not compare fitted exponents, compute-optimal splits, parameter-counting conventions, or fitting methods.

rows.subject: ONE model
rows.operation_detail: Fit a power law to open-loop normalized trajectory ADE across training-data scales.

conditions.value: The paper describes scales of 10 thousand, 50 thousand, 0.2 million, 0.7 million, 2 million, and 4 million demonstrations; the subsection says five models.

rows.measure: Normalized trajectory ADE; log-transformed data fit, reported as Y = 0.6833 · X −0.188, r = −0.963.
rows.note: The authors interpret the strong negative correlation as a power-law relationship between data amount and trajectory-fitting error. The displayed equation is transcribed as it appears in the supplied text.
rows.check: Held-out ADE is a regression error close to the training objective, so it is a fair analogue of held-out loss for V5. The fit Y = 0.6833·X^-0.188 (r = -0.963) uses five or six points over about 2.6 orders of magnitude, with no uncertainty. The text says 'five models' but lists six sizes. It is not a V7 result: no fitting choices are compared.

rows.subject: ONE model
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate closed-loop safety score across training-data scales.
rows.note: The text says safety improves rapidly at first, then growth slows within the 200k-to-700k-data range; the authors do not describe a stable power-law relationship.
rows.check: The closed-loop safety score is a deployment task score, not a held-out loss. It is also not a language-model downstream task, so it fits no version. Values are figure-only. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.note: The text says comfort improves rapidly at first, then growth slows within the 200k-to-700k-data range; the authors do not describe a stable power-law relationship.
rows.check: Same as r2: a closed-loop comfort score, figure-only, no power-law fit attempted.

rows.subject: ONE model
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate weighted total closed-loop score across training-data scales.
rows.note: The authors explicitly conclude that the open-loop metric has a power-law relationship but the closed-loop metric does not.
rows.check: Total closed-loop score. The authors say it differs from the open-loop power law but give no fit or values. The closed-loop test set is also not aligned with the open-loop set. It does not bear on V7, which concerns fitting or setup choices for the same quantity, not a different metric.

relationships.condition: Open-loop held-out ADE vs number of demonstrations (10k–4M) for the ONE imitation-learning driving model
relationships.reason: Log-log fit Y = 0.6833·X^-0.188, r = -0.963 (r1). It rests on few points with no uncertainty reported.
relationships.display_finding: Held-out displacement error followed Y=0.6833·X^−0.188 with correlation −0.963, based on few points without reported uncertainty.

reader_labels.reason: The study reports an open-loop ADE power-law fit across training-data scales (r1).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that the closed-loop metric does not show the open-loop power-law relationship (r7); individual closed-loop metrics have differing trends and growth patterns (r2-r6).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Open-loop versus closed-loop evaluation of the same driving model family
